| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

[LLM] TOCTOU tamper of VS Code Remote-SSH bootstrap script in user temp by non-VS-Code Weaponization Medium
Hunts non-VS-Code processes writing or modifying shell scripts in the user-writable temp / .vscode-server staging paths that VS Code's Remote-SSH extension uses to generate the bootstrap script. This is the exact TOCTOU window the disclosed RCE abuses: an attacker on a compromised developer workstation races to inject payload into the bootstrap before it is shipped to the remote cloud host. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused artefact ('bootstrap shell script' written to a 'user-writable temporary directory' then transferred and executed on the remote SSH target). The high-signal pivot is a NON-VS-Code process touching those paths — VS Code itself is the only legitimate writer to its own staging area. Cross-checked with VS Code Remote-SSH source paths (.vscode-server, vscode-ssh-askpass, %TEMP%) and Microsoft's documented design statement that mitigation is left to users — so SOCs must catch the tamper, not rely on a patch. Cross-checked against: • https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/ssh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.004 T1554

| where FileName endswith ".sh" or FileName has_any ("bootstrap","install","askpass")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","ssh.exe","sshd.exe","node.exe"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft VS Code\", @"\Cursor\", @"\.vscode\"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\.vscode-server\", "vscode-remote-ssh", "vscode-ssh-askpass", "/tmp/vscode-ssh")

| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code Remote-SSH Bootstrap Script Tampered By Non-VS-Code Process
id: 8a3f1c9b-2b41-4a5d-9e88-1f6c7d4a9b21
description: Detects writes/modifications to VS Code Remote-SSH bootstrap scripts or askpass helpers in user-writable temp paths by processes other than the VS Code / Cursor / OpenSSH binary set. Targets the TOCTOU window in the disclosed Remote-SSH RCE chain.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/vs-code-remote-ssh-rce/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1546
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1554
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\.vscode-server\'
      - 'vscode-remote-ssh'
      - 'vscode-ssh-askpass'
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.sh'
      - 'bootstrap'
      - 'askpass'
  filter_legit_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
      - '\ssh.exe'
      - '\sshd.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  condition: selection_path and selection_name and not filter_legit_proc
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\.vscode-server\\* OR *vscode-remote-ssh* OR *vscode-ssh-askpass* OR */tmp/vscode-ssh*)) AND (@TargetFilename:(*.sh OR *bootstrap* OR *askpass*)) AND -@Image:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\ssh.exe OR *\\sshd.exe OR *\\node.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|\\\.vscode-server\\|vscode-remote-ssh|vscode-ssh-askpass|\/tmp\/vscode-ssh)/i
| TargetFileName=/(\.sh$|bootstrap|askpass)/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(Code|Cursor|ssh|sshd|node)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| _count > 0
ENDPOINT

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

[LLM] External-tenant Teams CallParticipantDetail (vishing first-contact) Delivery Medium
Hunts unsolicited Teams calls/chats originating from an external or federated tenant — the documented first-contact step of the Quick Assist vishing chain. Pivots on the CallParticipantDetail operation in the MicrosoftTeams workload of the Unified Audit Log. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim 'CallParticipantDetail' operation under the 'MicrosoftTeams' workload — the single highest-value forensic artifact called out by Maurice Fielenbach/DART. Federated/external/guest participant flags convert a noisy event into a vishing first-contact signal. Cross-checked Microsoft Purview Teams audit-log reference and the MSTIC Storm-1811 / Black Basta Quick Assist advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-teams-audit-log-events • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/

[LLM] Quick Assist / RMM launch within 30 min of external Teams contact Installation High
Correlates an external-tenant CallParticipantDetail event with a Quick Assist (quickassist.exe / msra.exe) or other RMM launch on the recipient's device inside a 30-minute window — the documented Black Basta / Storm-1811 attack pattern referenced in the article. Rationale: The article calls out 'Quick Assist launch' as a documented vishing pivot and references the 2024 Black Basta affiliate campaign that weaponised exactly this pattern. Pairing the article's exact 'CallParticipantDetail' artifact with quickassist.exe/msra.exe (Microsoft-signed RMM tools) inside a 30-min window converts two noisy signals into a high-fidelity chain. Cross-checked MSTIC Storm-1811 advisory and Rapid7 Black Basta write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2024/05/10/ongoing-social-engineering-campaign-refreshes-payloads/

| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner ExtTeamsContact on $left.AccountObjectId == $right.AccountObjectId
| where Timestamp between (CallTime .. CallTime + WindowMin)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, CallTime)
| project CallTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by ProcessTime desc

[LLM] Microsoft enrichment: TeamsImpersonationDetected / SecurityRiskInCallDetected Delivery High
Surfaces Microsoft's own Teams enrichment signals (TeamsImpersonationDetected, SecurityRiskInCallDetected) called out in the article as supplementary indicators. These are first-party Microsoft Threat Intel verdicts on the Teams call/chat and warrant immediate triage. Rationale: Anchors on the two enrichment-signal operation names verbatim from the article ('TeamsImpersonationDetected' and 'SecurityRiskInCallDetected'). These are Microsoft-provided verdicts so FP rate is low and signal quality high. Cross-checked Microsoft Purview Teams audit-log event reference. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-teams-audit-log-events

title: Microsoft Teams Impersonation or Security Risk Enrichment Signal
id: 4d2b9b6c-7f1a-4e0e-9a8e-2c1f4a9d5e3b
description: Microsoft's first-party Teams enrichment events (TeamsImpersonationDetected / SecurityRiskInCallDetected) indicating a likely vishing / IT-helpdesk impersonation call.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

  - attack.t1656
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit
detection:
  selection:
    Workload: MicrosoftTeams
    Operation:
      - TeamsImpersonationDetected
      - SecurityRiskInCallDetected
  condition: selection
level: high
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:(TeamsImpersonationDetected OR SecurityRiskInCallDetected)
APPLICATION
`o365_management_activity` Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation IN ("TeamsImpersonationDetected","SecurityRiskInCallDetected") | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, max(_time) as lastSeen, values(UserId) as user, values(ClientIP) as srcIP, values(Operation) as ops, count by Id, OrganizationId | sort - firstSeen
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-29 18 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign used malicious npm packages to target cloud and CI/CD credentials across developer environments. This report details the attack chain, detection opportunities, and mitigation guidance to help organizations identify and disrupt related activity. The post Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT1059.001 T1195.002 T1204.002 T1219 T1486
Domainsaab.sportsontheweb.net
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] vpmdhaj typosquat npm package install via preinstall hook (node child of npm) · [LLM] Bun runtime download from github.com/oven-sh during npm install (Gen-2 loader) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] payload.bin written under node_modules by node process · [LLM] __DAEMONIZED=1 environment marker on spawned process · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTP beacon to vpmdhaj C2 (aab.sportsontheweb.net) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cloud metadata service hit (IMDSv2 / ECS) from node process under node_modules · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] vpmdhaj typosquat npm package install via preinstall hook (node child of npm) Delivery High
Detects execution of the malicious vpmdhaj cluster of typosquat packages during npm install. Anchors on the exact package names published 2026-05-28 plus the preinstall/postinstall/install lifecycle hook tokens carried in the node command line. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package names and lifecycle-hook tokens documented in Microsoft's article (Block 1 in source) plus the Gen-1/Gen-2 stager filenames (preinstall.js, setup.mjs, opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js). Stagers run as a node child of npm during install — pairing process/parent narrows scope to the actual attack path, not generic npm telemetry.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd", "npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper",
    "preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js"
  )
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd", "\\npx.cmd")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd")
| where CommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where CommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper",
    "preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    - '/npm'

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\npm.cmd OR */node OR */npm) OR @process.executable.path:(*/node OR */npm)) (@CommandLine:(*preinstall* OR *postinstall* OR *"npm install"*) OR @process.command_line:(*preinstall* OR *postinstall* OR *"npm install"*)) (@CommandLine:(*@vpmdhaj* OR *opensearch-setup* OR *opensearch-config-utility* OR *opensearch-security-scanner* OR *elastic-opensearch-helper* OR *search-engine-setup* OR *env-config-manager* OR *preinstall.js* OR *setup.mjs* OR *opensearch_init.js* OR *ai_init.js*) OR @process.command_line:(*@vpmdhaj* OR *opensearch-setup* OR *opensearch-config-utility* OR *opensearch-security-scanner* OR *elastic-opensearch-helper* OR *search-engine-setup* OR *env-config-manager* OR *preinstall.js* OR *setup.mjs* OR *opensearch_init.js* OR *ai_init.js*))

| CommandLine=/(preinstall|postinstall|npm install)/i
| CommandLine=/(@vpmdhaj|opensearch-setup|opensearch-config-utility|opensearch-security-scanner|elastic-opensearch-helper|search-engine-setup|env-config-manager|preinstall\.js|setup\.mjs|opensearch_init\.js|ai_init\.js)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*preinstall*","*postinstall*","*npm install*") AND Processes.process IN ("*@vpmdhaj*","*opensearch-setup*","*opensearch-setup-tool*","*opensearch-config-utility*","*opensearch-security-scanner*","*elastic-opensearch-helper*","*search-engine-setup*","*env-config-manager*","*devops-tools*","*search-setup*","*elastic-helper*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] payload.bin written under node_modules by node process Installation High
Detects the Gen-1 stager dropping the ~195 KB Bun-compiled second-stage binary as payload.bin inside the package install directory beneath node_modules. The combination of filename, parent directory, and node initiating process is article-specific and very high fidelity. Rationale: Block 2 in the article literally is this detection — payload.bin name + node_modules path + node initiator is exactly the Gen-1 drop. Filename is too generic on its own (any backup or game asset could be called payload.bin) but combined with node_modules + node initiator the FP rate collapses.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "payload.bin"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd", "npx.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName =~ "payload.bin"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "npm", "npx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize,
          TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: vpmdhaj payload.bin Drop Under node_modules
id: 9d1b53e4-aa3f-4d92-8bd1-1f7e7c84d5c2
description: Detects the Gen-1 vpmdhaj stager writing payload.bin (the ~195 KB Bun-compiled stage-2) into a node_modules directory during npm install.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

selection_path:

selection_proc:
  Image|endswith:
    - '\node.exe'
    - '\npm.cmd'
    - '\npx.cmd'
    - '/node'
    - '/npm'
condition: selection_name and selection_path and selection_proc
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:*\payload.bin @TargetFilename:*node_modules* @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\npm.cmd OR *\npx.cmd)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\payload\.bin$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/payload\.bin$/i
| TargetFileName=/node_modules/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(\\node\.exe|\\npm\.cmd|\\npx\.cmd|\/node|\/npm)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="payload.bin" AND Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="payload.bin" AND Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*" AND Filesystem.action="created") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Outbound HTTP beacon to vpmdhaj C2 (aab.sportsontheweb.net) Command & Control High
Detects the Gen-1 stager's HTTP C2 beacon and stage-2 download from the vpmdhaj-controlled domain. Scopes the connection on the C2 hostname plus node as the initiating process so non-developer traffic is excluded. Rationale: aab.sportsontheweb.net is the only IOC the article surfaces as a Gen-1 C2 host. Scoping on the FQDN (rather than the X-Supply header, which is not consistently captured in standard CEF / ASIM columns) gives a clean, high-fidelity detection that survives across DNS, proxy, and EDR network telemetry.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "aab.sportsontheweb.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith "sportsontheweb.net"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Host = "aab.sportsontheweb.net";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where DestinationHostName has C2Host
          or RequestURL has C2Host
          or DestinationDnsDomain has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName,
               RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, RequestMethod,
               SentBytes, ReceivedBytes, DeviceProduct),
  (ImWebSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Url has C2Host or DstHostname has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname,
               Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpMethod,
               HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpResponseBodyBytes, EventProduct),
  (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where Name has C2Host
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Outbound Connection to vpmdhaj C2 Domain

[LLM] __DAEMONIZED=1 environment marker on spawned process Installation High
Detects the vpmdhaj stage-2 binary's self-re-entry guard, which sets __DAEMONIZED=1 in the environment of the detached child to avoid double-spawning. This env-var name is unique to this campaign per Microsoft's writeup. Rationale: Block 3 in the article — the __DAEMONIZED=1 string is a unique campaign artifact called out explicitly in Microsoft's writeup as the re-entry guard. The literal string is not a known legitimate environment variable in any common runtime so single-string match is sufficient.
ATT&CKT1543 T1564
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or AdditionalFields has "__DAEMONIZED"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "__DAEMONIZED=1"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cloud metadata service hit (IMDSv2 / ECS) from node process under node_modules Actions on Objectives High
Detects the stage-2 credential harvester's queries against AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) and ECS task-role metadata (169.254.170.2) when the originating process is node — particularly when launched from a node_modules path. Pairs the EDR-side metadata fetch with the CloudTrail-side STS/SecretsManager fan-out for correlation. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 (IMDSv2) and 169.254.170.2 (ECS task role) are the exact metadata endpoints the article names. Pairing the link-local destination with a node/bun initiating process is the article-specific anchor; the CloudTrail companion query catches the fan-out across 16+ regions (GetCallerIdentity → AssumeRole → ListSecrets/GetSecretValue) called out as a defining behaviour of the stage-2 harvester.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528 T1555.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "bun.exe", "bun")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js", "payload.bin")
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ParentCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5),
            ParentPaths = make_set(InitiatingProcessFolderPath, 5)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| where SrcUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: AWS IMDSv2 / ECS Metadata Hit From Node
id: a7c91d54-2f8e-4b3a-9c1d-5e8f7a3b6c20
description: Detects an outbound connection to the AWS instance-metadata service (169.254.169.254) or ECS task-role metadata endpoint (169.254.170.2) initiated by a node / bun process — a signature of the vpmdhaj stage-2 credential harvester.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/typosquatted-npm-packages-used-steal-cloud-ci-cd-secrets/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1555.006
logsource:
  category: network_connection
selection_ip:
  DestinationIp:
    - '169.254.169.254'
    - '169.254.170.2'
selection_proc:
  Image|endswith:
    - '\node.exe'
    - '\bun.exe'
    - '/node'
    - '/bun'
condition: selection_ip and selection_proc
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:(169.254.169.254 OR 169.254.170.2) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^169\.254\.(169\.254|170\.2)$/
| ContextImageFileName=/(\\node\.exe|\\bun\.exe|\/node|\/bun)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, sourceIPAddress, userAgent, awsRegion
| filter eventName in ["GetCallerIdentity", "AssumeRole", "ListSecrets", "GetSecretValue"]
  and userIdentity.type in ["AssumedRole", "IAMUser", "WebIdentityUser"]
  and (userAgent like /aws-sdk-js/i or userAgent like /node/i or userAgent like /Bun/i)
| stats count() as call_count,
        count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_events,
        count_distinct(awsRegion) as distinct_regions,
        earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen,
        latest(@timestamp) as last_seen
        by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter distinct_regions >= 5 and distinct_events >= 2
| sort call_count desc

[LLM] Bun runtime download from github.com/oven-sh during npm install (Gen-2 loader) Delivery Medium
Detects the Gen-2 stager's hallmark: an npm-driven node process fetching a legitimate Bun runtime release (v1.3.13) directly from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases as a loader for the bundled stage-2 payload. The combination of source (npm install) + destination (oven-sh/bun release asset) is the article-specific signal. Rationale: The article names github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases v1.3.13 as the legitimate-but-abused payload host for the Gen-2 setup.mjs loader. github.com is trusted egress so destination alone is too noisy; pairing it with a node/npm initiating process during install lifecycle bounds the FP rate to actual Bun adopters.
ATT&CKT1105 T1218
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install", "node_modules")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "github.com" and Url has "oven-sh/bun"
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "npm", "npx")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install", "node_modules")
  ) on $left.DvcHostname == $right.DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, TimeGenerated1)) <= 300
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, DstHostname,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PhantomMail: Ukrainian-themed ZIP/RAR delivered via Google Drive or 4sync links Delivery Medium
Hunts GreyVibe's PhantomMail vector: spear-phishing emails with ZIP/RAR attachments or body links to Google Drive / 4sync, themed against Ukrainian gov, emergency, telecom or energy entities. Pivots on archive attachments plus the two specific cloud-storage URL families called out by WithSecure. Rationale: Anchors on WithSecure-stated PhantomMail strings: ZIP/RAR archives, Google Drive and 4sync links, and Ukrainian gov/emergency/telecom/energy lure impersonation. Mail-only signal so endpoint queries are deferred to the execution UCs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] PhantomClick: browser → mshta/powershell/cmd within 60s of fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS lure Exploitation High
Hunts the PhantomClick ClickFix flow: victim visits a fake Zoom or LAPAS site, the page displays a fake Cloudflare verification, and the user pastes a self-infecting command. Pivots on a browser parent spawning interpreter children within seconds, with the cmdline carrying ClickFix-style payload markers. Rationale: Maps directly to WithSecure's PhantomClick description: fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS verification leading users to paste self-infecting commands. Combines browser parent + interpreter child + ClickFix telltale strings (Cloudflare, ray-id, captcha, lapas, Verify you are human). Cross-checked against MITRE T1204.001 and recurring ClickFix Sigma rules to ensure novelty. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] GreyVibe: RDP enablement via fDenyTSConnections=0 + firewall by PowerShell RAT Installation High
Hunts LegionRelay's 'RDP access setup' capability: PowerShell or cmd flipping fDenyTSConnections to 0, enabling UserAuthentication, or opening the RDP firewall rule. Article explicitly calls out RDP access setup as a LegionRelay function and the attacker uses PowerShell-based RATs. Rationale: WithSecure: 'LegionRelay supports … RDP access setup.' Anchors on the canonical Windows knobs an attacker has to flip to enable RDP on a previously-disabled host: fDenyTSConnections=0 registry value, UserAuthentication relax, and the RemoteDesktop firewall group. Gated on a scripting-host parent because the article describes the actor as PowerShell-based. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/004/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] PowerShell.exe sustained beaconing to uncategorized web endpoint (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay C2) Command & Control Medium
Hunts the LegionRelay/PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT C2 pattern: powershell.exe making repeated outbound HTTPS connections to a single rare external endpoint with no parent browser. Article describes both RATs as PowerShell-based with web C2 (UTC+3 panels, shared PrincessClub/DroneLink infra). Rationale: Both LegionRelay and PhantomRelay are described as PowerShell RATs and the C2 servers are on UTC+3 with web panels. Threshold + low-cardinality destination expresses 'beaconing' rather than one-shot egress. Doesn't reference specific IOCs from the article on purpose — actor rotates infra — but constrains pivot to powershell.exe initiated egress. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] GreyVibe cryptocurrency miner deployment via PowerShell RAT Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the cryptominer impact tail of the GreyVibe campaign: known miner binaries (xmrig, ethminer, t-rex, lolMiner) or Stratum protocol egress from victim machines. Article explicitly notes a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines. Rationale: WithSecure: 'a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines.' Anchors on the well-known XMRig/RandomX family + Stratum protocol strings + canonical mining pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) and pool domains. Article didn't ship a specific miner SHA so we rely on family-level indicators. Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
