Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware known SHA256 file/process sightings · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware command-line argument signature · [LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware --full dual child relaunch (--system + --shares) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The Gentlemen ransomware: Dissecting a self-propagating Go encryptor
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Gentlemen ransomware SYSTEM elevation via gentlemen_system scheduled task · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Gentlemen ransomware SYSTEM elevation via gentlemen_system scheduled task Installation High
Detects The Gentlemen ransomware's privilege-escalation sequence: it deletes any existing scheduled task named gentlemen_system, then creates a new one-time task running its binary under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and triggers it. The literal task name is a strong unique-string signal. Rationale: gentlemen_system is the literal, hardcoded scheduled-task name documented in the Microsoft analysis of Storm-2697's encryptor; combined with schtasks.exe parent it is article-specific and not a generic schtasks alert. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1548
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "gentlemen_system"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create", "/delete", "/run")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "gentlemen_system"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/create", "/delete", "/run")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, Domain = SubjectDomainName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware command-line argument signature Exploitation High
Hunts for processes invoked with the unique combination of command-line flags exposed by Storm-2697's Gentlemen encryptor (--password, --full, --system, --shares, --spread, --ultrafast, --superfast). These flags are documented in the author's own usage banner and are atypical for legitimate Go binaries. Rationale: These flag names come straight from the article's documented usage prompt for the binary (Figure 2, Table 1). The combination of --password + any of {full,spread,shares,system,ultrafast,superfast} is essentially never seen on legitimate software because The Gentlemen invents its own argument grammar. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/the-gentlemen-ransomware-dissecting-a-self-propagating-go-encryptor/
ATT&CKT1059 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--password"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--full", "--spread", "--shares", "--system", "--ultrafast", "--superfast", "--silent", "--wipe", "--keep")
| extend FlagCount = countof(ProcessCommandLine, "--")
| where FlagCount >= 2
| extend BadPasswordMatch = ProcessCommandLine has "9VoAvR7G"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, BadPasswordMatch
| order by BadPasswordMatch desc, Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "--password"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--full", "--spread", "--shares", "--system", "--ultrafast", "--superfast", "--silent", "--wipe", "--keep")
| extend KnownPassword = iff(CommandLine has "9VoAvR7G", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName,
          ParentProcessName, CommandLine, KnownPassword
| order by KnownPassword desc, TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware --full dual child relaunch (--system + --shares) Exploitation High
Detects the ransomware's documented --full operating mode where the parent binary spawns two children of itself: one with --system (local volume encryption under a SYSTEM scheduled task) and one with --shares (mapped network drives / UNC encryption in the user session). The same image hash appearing as both parent and two children within seconds is a high-fidelity execution-tree signature. Rationale: The article documents this exact behaviour: `--full` mode causes the binary to spawn two children of itself, one appended with `--system` (encrypts local drives via scheduled task) and one with `--shares` (encrypts UNC/mapped drives in user session). The dual-child same-PPID shape on a single host is an article-specific TTP not present in generic ransomware rules. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/the-gentlemen-ransomware-dissecting-a-self-propagating-go-encryptor/
ATT&CKT1106 T1486 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let lookback = 7d;
let children = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--system", "--shares")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--full"
    | extend Mode = case(ProcessCommandLine has "--system", "system",
                          ProcessCommandLine has "--shares", "shares",
                          "other")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
              ChildFile = FileName,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              Mode, InitiatingProcessId;
children
| summarize Modes = make_set(Mode),
            FirstTime = min(Timestamp),
            LastTime = max(Timestamp),
            ChildCmds = make_set(ChildCmd, 5),
            ChildHashes = make_set(ChildSHA256, 5)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, ParentSHA256, ParentCmd, InitiatingProcessId
| where array_length(Modes) >= 2
| order by FirstTime desc
let lookback = 7d;
let children = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any ("--system", "--shares")
    | where ParentProcessName != ""
    | extend Mode = case(CommandLine has "--system", "system",
                          CommandLine has "--shares", "shares",
                          "other");
let parents = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has "--full"
    | project ParentTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, ParentPid = NewProcessId,
              ParentImage = NewProcessName, ParentCmd = CommandLine;
children
| join kind=inner parents on Computer, $left.ProcessId == $right.ParentPid
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ParentImage, ParentCmd,
          ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine, Mode, Account = SubjectUserName
| summarize Modes = make_set(Mode), FirstTime = min(TimeGenerated), LastTime = max(TimeGenerated),
            ChildCmds = make_set(ChildCmd, 5)
            by Computer, ParentImage, ParentCmd, Account
| where array_length(Modes) >= 2
| order by FirstTime desc
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentCommandLine:*--full* @CommandLine:(*--system* OR *--shares*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("--(system|shares)\\b", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| ParentCommandLine = ParentBaseFileName
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("--full\\b", field=CommandLine, flags="i") | rename(TargetProcessId, as=ParentPid) | rename(aid, as=parent_aid)}, field=[aid, ParentProcessId], key=[parent_aid, ParentPid])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentPid], function={ collect([CommandLine]) | count(as=cnt) })

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Gogs RCE: git rebase invoked with --exec flag (argument injection) Exploitation High
Detects the Gogs zero-day argument-injection RCE in flight: the Gogs server process invokes 'git rebase' with an attacker-controlled branch name that smuggles a '--exec=' flag, causing arbitrary command execution as the Gogs user. The smoking gun is a 'git rebase' process whose command line contains '--exec' (or '-x') and whose parent is the gogs binary. Rationale: The article explicitly names the injected flag ('--exec') and the abused command path ('git rebase' during 'Rebase before merging'), with the Gogs server as the parent that invokes git. A 'git rebase' process whose parent is gogs and whose argv contains '--exec' has effectively no legitimate use — the Gogs codebase never legitimately passes --exec to rebase. Cross-referenced with Rapid7's earlier Gogs argument-injection family (CVE-2024-39930/39932/39933) which the article explicitly compares this flaw to. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/securing-developer-tools-unpatched-code-vulnerabilities-in-gogs-1 • https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/securing-developer-tools-unpatched-code-vulnerabilities-in-gogs-2 • https://thehackernews.com/2024/07/critical-vulnerabilities-disclosed-in.html • https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7777
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "gogs"
| where FileName =~ "git"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rebase"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--exec", "-x=", "--exec=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GogsCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GitCmd  = ProcessCommandLine,
          GitPath = FolderPath,
          ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/gogs" or ParentProcessName =~ "gogs"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/git" or ActingProcessName =~ "git"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "rebase"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--exec", "-x=", "--exec=")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          GogsCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
          GitCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Gogs Argument Injection via git rebase --exec
id: 7c4d2a2f-3e9a-4f2b-8b21-6d2bf4f1a5e1
description: Detects exploitation of the unpatched Gogs argument-injection RCE where a malicious pull-request branch name injects --exec into git rebase invoked by the Gogs server during Rebase-before-merging.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-gogs-zero-day-flaw-lets-hackers-get-remote-code-execution/
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1068
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '/gogs'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '/git'
    CommandLine|contains: 'rebase'
  selection_inject:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--exec'
      - '-x='
      - '--exec='
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_inject
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/git OR */bin/git) @process.command_line:(*rebase* AND (*--exec* OR *-x=* OR *--exec=*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^gogs$/i ImageFileName=/\/git$/i
| CommandLine=/rebase/i
| CommandLine=/(--exec|--exec=|\s-x=|\s-x\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="gogs" Processes.process_name="git" Processes.process="*rebase*" (Processes.process="*--exec*" OR Processes.process="* -x *" OR Processes.process="*-x=*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="gogs" Processes.process_name="git" Processes.process="*rebase*" (Processes.process="*--exec*" OR Processes.process="* -x *" OR Processes.process="*-x=*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Post-exploit shell or LOLBin spawned by git invoked from Gogs server Installation High
Follow-on detection for the Gogs --exec argument injection: once 'git rebase --exec=<cmd>' fires, git executes the attacker's command, producing a process tree of gogs -> git -> /bin/sh|bash|curl|wget|nc|python. Hunts for any non-git child of a git process whose parent is the Gogs server binary — the post-exploitation footprint the article describes ('compromise the server, dump credentials, pivot'). Rationale: The article enumerates the post-exploit objectives explicitly — 'compromise the server, read every repository on the instance, dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets), pivot to other network-accessible systems'. Git itself has zero legitimate reason to spawn shells, network tools, or interpreters; in the Gogs server context, git only invokes other git plumbing binaries. Any non-git child of git on a Gogs host is the --exec payload landing. Confirmed pattern matches Rapid7's documented Gogs argument-injection family (CVE-2024-39930/39932/39933). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/securing-developer-tools-unpatched-code-vulnerabilities-in-gogs-1 • https://thehackernews.com/2024/07/critical-vulnerabilities-disclosed-in.html • https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerabilities-threats/attackers-exploited-gogs-zero-day-months
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1505.003 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let GogsHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "gogs" and FileName =~ "git"
    | distinct DeviceId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (GogsHosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "git"
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "gogs"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","socat","base64","chmod","id","whoami","uname","cat","openssl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ChildProc = FileName,
          ChildCmd  = ProcessCommandLine,
          GitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GogsCmd   = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/git" or ParentProcessName =~ "git"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","socat","base64","chmod","id","whoami","uname","cat")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "rebase" or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("--exec","-x=")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ChildProc = ActingProcessName,
          ChildCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          GitCmd    = ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd") or SHA1 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd") or MD5 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd") or SHA1 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd") or MD5 in~ ("d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["d8fcd57a71f9f6e55b063939dc7c1523660b7383", "efda81e1100ea977321d0f2eeb0dfa7a6b132abd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud worm GitHub Action workflow file dropped under .github/workflows · [LLM] npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall hook spawning credential-harvest tooling · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Cyberhaven trojanized Chrome extension C2 callback to cyberhavenext.pro · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfil to filev2.getsession.org · [LLM] postmark-mcp BCC exfil to giftshop.club · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Cyberhaven trojanized Chrome extension C2 callback to cyberhavenext.pro Command & Control High
Hunts for DNS/HTTPS resolution to cyberhavenext.pro from Chromium-based browsers — the C2 domain used by the malicious Cyberhaven Chrome extension (v24.10.4, active 25–26 Dec 2024) and ~35 related extensions in the Secure Annex cluster. The extension's worker.js fetched its config from this host before exfiltrating cookies and authenticated sessions. Rationale: Article names cyberhavenext.pro as an explicit IOC. Cross-checked against Cyberhaven's own engineering blog, Secure Annex's cluster analysis, Darktrace and Obsidian Security write-ups — all confirm the domain as the C2 used by the malicious worker.js bundled in extension v24.10.4 to retrieve config before stealing cookies/auth sessions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cyberhaven.com/engineering-blog/cyberhavens-preliminary-analysis-of-the-recent-malicious-chrome-extension • https://secureannex.com/blog/cyberhaven-extension-compromise/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/cyberhaven-supply-chain-attack-exploiting-browser-extensions • https://www.obsidiansecurity.com/resource/behind-the-breach-malicious-attack-on-cyberhavens-chrome-extension-developer-team
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1176 T1539
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr=DvcIpAddr),
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has_any (IOC) or DstHostname has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername=SrcUsername, Url, DstIpAddr)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm exfil to filev2.getsession.org Actions on Objectives High
Detects outbound traffic to filev2.getsession.org — the Session decentralised-network endpoint the Mini Shai-Hulud / Sha1-Hulud npm worm uses to exfil harvested GitHub, npm, cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, Docker and SSH credentials. Scopes to Node.js / package-manager process context so it doesn't fire on a real user running the Session messenger. Rationale: Article lists filev2.getsession.org in the IOC bundle. Cross-checked with Wiz (Mini Shai-Hulud), Socket (Tanstack packages), BleepingComputer and StepSecurity — all confirm Session's decentralized P2P file API as the exfil channel; gating on Node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun parent process distinguishes worm exfil from a real user's Session messenger traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-shai-hulud-malware-wave-compromises-600-npm-packages/

[LLM] Shai-Hulud worm GitHub Action workflow file dropped under .github/workflows Installation High
Detects file creation of shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml under any .github/workflows/ directory on a developer host. The Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms write this workflow then push it to a fresh branch so a PUSH-triggered Action exfiltrates harvested secrets. Rationale: Article references Mini Shai-Hulud and the postinstall credential-theft chain. Workflow filename triplet (shai-hulud-workflow.yml / shai-hulud.yaml / discussion.yaml) confirmed by Unit 42, Wiz, Datadog Security Labs and their public IOC repo. File-creation telemetry catches the worm during install-time, well before its GitHub push step. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0 • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1567.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let WormFiles = dynamic(["shai-hulud-workflow.yml","shai-hulud.yaml","shai-hulud.yml","discussion.yaml","discussion.yml"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ (WormFiles)
| where FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows" or FolderPath has "/.github/workflows"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let WormFiles = dynamic(["shai-hulud-workflow.yml","shai-hulud.yaml","shai-hulud.yml","discussion.yaml","discussion.yml"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ (WormFiles)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows" or TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] postmark-mcp BCC exfil to giftshop.club Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for outbound DNS/HTTPS to giftshop.club — the domain hosting phan@giftshop.club, the BCC recipient hard-coded into postmark-mcp v1.0.16 (the first publicly documented malicious npm-distributed MCP server, disclosed by Koi Security). Also catches BCC of organisational email to @giftshop.club via mail-flow telemetry. Rationale: Article lists giftshop.club in the IOC bundle. Koi Security (original disclosure), Snyk, BleepingComputer and the official Postmark advisory all confirm the BCC address phan@giftshop.club embedded in postmark-mcp v1.0.16. Detecting on the domain catches both the BCC mail leg (via Office mail-flow) and any local Node.js process resolving it during MCP server startup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft • https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-mcp-server-on-npm-postmark-mcp-harvests-emails/ • https://postmarkapp.com/blog/information-regarding-malicious-postmark-mcp-package • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/first-malicious-mcp-server-found.html
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.003 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Email.All_Email
let IOC = dynamic(["giftshop.club"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Actor=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Indicator=RemoteUrl, Path="network";
let Mail = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RecipientEmailAddress has_any (IOC) or SenderFromAddress has_any (IOC)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", Actor=SenderFromAddress, Process="", Cmd=Subject, Indicator=RecipientEmailAddress, Path="mail";
union Net, Mail
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["giftshop.club"]);
let Net = union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Path="dns"),
    (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has_any (IOC) or DstHostname has_any (IOC) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=SrcUsername, Indicator=coalesce(Url,DstHostname), Path="web");
let Mail = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Operation in ("Send","SendOnBehalf","SendAs") and (Recipients has "giftshop.club" or P2RecipientList has "giftshop.club" or P2Sender has "giftshop.club")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host="", Actor=UserId, Indicator=tostring(Recipients), Path="mail";
union Net, Mail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/yarn/pnpm postinstall hook spawning credential-harvest tooling Installation Medium
Hunts for package-manager processes (npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun) spawning TruffleHog, curl/wget reaching the Shai-Hulud or postmark-mcp exfil hosts, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js — the signature install-time payload chain used by the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 worms before EDR has a behavioural signal to bite on. Rationale: Article describes the npm postinstall credential-scraping chain (Mini Shai-Hulud, postmark-mcp). Datadog IOC repo, Wiz, Socket and Sysdig confirm setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js and TruffleHog binary execution from npm contexts as the post-compromise install-time signal — plus the webhook.site / filev2.getsession.org / giftshop.club exfil strings catch curl/wget invocations the worm chains. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://github.com/DataDog/indicators-of-compromise/tree/main/shai-hulud-2.0

title: Package-Manager Postinstall Hook Spawning Credential-Harvest Tooling
id: a1c7f4b3-8e6c-4f39-9a5b-4c9d0e1f6234
description: npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node/bun spawning trufflehog, or executing setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js, or reaching Shai-Hulud / postmark-mcp exfil hosts — the install-time payload chain documented across the Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 npm worm waves.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack
  - https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft
author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

detection:
  parent_pkg_mgr:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '/npm'
      - '/npx'
      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '/bun'
  child_susp_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\trufflehog.exe'
      - '\trufflehog'
      - '/trufflehog'
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_susp_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'setup_bun.js'
      - 'bun_environment.js'
      - 'trufflehog'
      - 'webhook.site'
      - 'filev2.getsession.org'
      - 'giftshop.club'

  - CI/CD pipelines that legitimately run trufflehog secret scanning inside npm scripts
  - Developers manually invoking trufflehog from a Node tool wrapper
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\Npm.exe OR *\npx.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\bun.exe) (@Image:(*\trufflehog.exe OR *\TruffleHog.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*setup_bun.js* OR *bun_environment.js* OR *trufflehog* OR *TruffleHog* OR *webhook.site* OR *filev2.getsession.org* OR *giftshop.club*))

| ImageFileName=/(trufflehog|curl|wget|bun)(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(setup_bun\.js|bun_environment\.js|trufflehog|webhook\.site|filev2\.getsession\.org|giftshop\.club)/i

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Carnival Cruise confirms data breach affecting nearly 6 million people

BleepingComputer
2026-05-28 7 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Carnival Corporation, the world's largest cruise line operator, has confirmed a data breach affecting nearly 6 million people claimed by the ShinyHunters extortion gang in April 2026. [...]

ATT&CKT1190 T1486
Domainscarnivalcorp.com
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Detected
